open_questions: Centroid remains inconclusive because no sector shows a clear difference image at T=11.98; ground-based multicolour transit photometry or high-resolution imaging within 1 px (21 arcsec) is needed to definitively locate the dip on the M-dwarf vs the 1.8 arcsec neighbour that could cause it with ~0.14 eclipse.
dossier.public_summary: A 15-day, flat-bottomed 3.5 h dip repeats three times with the same depth, no odd-even difference and no secondary. The low rank from a blend predictor reflects a nearby star that could mimic the dip, but difference imaging cannot locate it and the transit shape and consistency favour a 3.9 Earth-radius planet around a nearby M dwarf.

reasons.why: Flat-bottomed transit, not V-shaped, favours planet over grazing binary.
Odd and even depths identical (3738 vs 3735 ppm), no binary at twice period.
No significant secondary eclipse; below 5 and below best_brightening_snr, rules against stellar companion.

Centroid has no clear image (too shallow for difference imaging at T=11.98), so cannot prove on-target; a neighbour at 1.8 arcsec could cause dip with 0.1404 eclipse, but xgboost planet_rank 0.11 would weight this heavily if on-target favours were not offsetting. Absence of secondary, flat shape and transit-depth consistency remain positive on-target evidence.
All 3 transits have consistent depth (3736 ppm, no outliers) and depth steady across sectors (3778 ppm vs 3674 ppm), argues against a few bad events or NEB.

Period is ~2.55x measured spot period (5.866 d) but phase_curve amplitude 389.6 ppm is small vs depth 3732 ppm and shape is transit-like, so coincidence by chance not strong; M-dwarf variability alone does not create a flat 3.89 Rearth signal.
